A positive-radius negative interval exists iff q(θ)>c=2sqrt(a(2a+b)). The cosine angular locus has no directions if q+≤c, all directions if q->c (one annular negative band), otherwise exactly two antipodal arcs (two lobes), including the strict-boundary q-=c. Angular averaging removes the cosine and is negative somewhere iff a/b>(3+sqrt7)/4. Exact ray substitutions give equal-rate birth t=0.238562694451… and 2:1 annulus splitting t=0.172753380808…. Independent numerical tests checked the inequalities at seven rate pairs; the classification is established by the exact quadratic and connected angular arcs, not grid sampling.
